sources.title: Crypto worth billions frozen after suspected Binance hack - BBC
passages: Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have also frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."

Early checks show the suspected hack may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said in a series of online alerts.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of assets.
"It does look like a hack," Binance's former boss Changpeng Zhao said on X.
Binance said earlier that the amount of funds frozen may continue to increase while investigations are underway.
Binance, which was founded in China by Zhao in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The incident is potentially the biggest ever crypto heist, eclipsing a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, which was linked to North Korea.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses".

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of assets. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses". Early checks show the suspected hack may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said in a series of online alerts. The incident is potentially the biggest ever crypto heist, eclipsing a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, which was linked to North Korea. The security incident concerns Binance.com, while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US which provides trading services specifically for American residents, said its platform is not affected by the issue. "It does look like a hack," Binance's former boss Changpeng Zhao said on X. Zhao, who is also known as CZ, no longer manages the firm but remains a key shareholder. Binance said earlier that the amount of funds frozen may continue to increase while investigations are underway. "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice," Binance said, urging users to rely only on its official channels for updates. It added that it will release a full report once its investigation is complete. In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing their assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have also frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his firm is "closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance" and that his company has frozen more than $800m in assets linked to the incident. Circle is the issuer and co-creator of the USDC, one of the world's largest US dollar-backed cryptocurrencies. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack." "Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority," said Ardoino, whose company issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Binance, which was founded in China by Zhao in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under custody. Prosecutors had accused Pleterski of stealing tens of millions of dollars of investor funds to buy himself a range of luxuries. Police say Faisa Ali used cash from unsuspecting investors for jewellery, homeware and fast food. Javier Milei had denied acting fraudulently when a cryptocurrency nosedived after he deleted a social media post about it. AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.

The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, 1 Live Activities, and Siri AI.
2 And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes.
An enhanced six-speaker sound system now provides 50 percent deeper bass and remarkable sound clarity for even more immersive audio.
2 It is available to pre-order starting today, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.
“PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display.
It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
PROLED XDR offers pros a super-wide color gamut with P3 and now Adobe RGB — critical for workflows in photography and design — along with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges.
2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading.
Cutting-edge factory calibration ensures luminance, white point, and color gamut are precisely aligned with standard targets.
Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them.
7 And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so apps perform at incredible speed.
The new MacBook Pro comes to life with macOS 27.

Siri AI can draw on personal context to help pros find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections.

Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence by using a dedicated keyboard shortcut to get help with a specific item.
Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display.
And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience.
3 In addition, storage is now configurable up to 16TB.
Updated system gesture APIs also enable developers to create intuitive experiences designed specifically for Touch.

These include everyday productivity and collaboration apps like Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook; powerful creative tools for photo and video editing like Adobe Lightroom and DaVinci Resolve; 3D modeling and animation apps like Blender, Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon ZBrush, and Shapr3D; along with music apps like Algoriddim djay Pro.
Spatial Audio with Dolby Atmos wraps users in immersive sound for music and movies, and studio-quality mics deliver clean, clear audio for calls, recordings, and voice commands.

It is made with 55 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors.
It is manufactured with 45 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain.
As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.
Both deliver phenomenal single- and multithreaded CPU performance, along with faster unified memory, giving users blazing speed for the most demanding workflows.

M5 Pro offers game-changing performance for scientists, engineers, software developers, and creative pros tackling intensive projects, accelerating everything from compiling code and running AI tasks to sequencing DNA and editing multiple streams of 8K ProRes video.
M5 Max is built for users who want to push the limits even further, including 3D VFX artists, AI developers, and film composers.

With M5 Max, pros can run LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device and accelerate intense workflows across detailed visual effects, 3D animation projects, film scores, and 8K video post-production.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro now weighs half a pound less at 3 pounds, while the 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs just 4 pounds — 0.7 pounds lighter than before.

With all the fuss about Apple finally releasing a touchscreen MacBook Pro , you may have forgotten about the new model's other key display technology: OLED, or what Apple calls PROLED XDR. It's typical of Apple to change a standard tech term to a cringy marketing-focused name, but in this case, the "PRO" designation appears to be justified. The new MacBook Pros are squarely aimed at photographers, artists and video editors who can justify the high price for a high-quality touch display. To appeal to those folks, Apple didn't just integrate a touch feature and OLED display and call it a day. Rather, it built what looks like one of the best pro laptop displays ever, with high brightness and contrast, excellent color accuracy and even a display engine that adapts to a pixel's age. For the new models, Apple used tandem OLED technology (first employed on the M4 iPad Pro) that stacks multiple organic layers into a single display panel. Judging by an Apple graphic in its press release, it appears to use a triangular pixel arrangement and not a striped RGB OLED system that can offer sharper text (we've reached out to the company for clarification on that). There are several key benefits to tandem OLED tech, namely high peak HDR brightness, a lower burn-in risk and a longer panel lifespan. It's also brighter and more color-accurate when viewed from an angle. At the same time, it retains and even improves the primary benefit of OLED displays: extremely high contrast. Apple says that the new MacBook Pros with PROLED XDR deliver up to 2,000 nits peak HDR, compared to 1,600 nits peak HDR for current models with Mini LED tech. That's very high for an OLED display and at least as bright or brighter than any other OLED laptop on the market (if accurate). Apple also touts an "industry-leading" 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, much higher than current MacBook Pro models. The PROLED XDR screens also offer high color accuracy. Apple says the new models now cover both the P3 (HDR) and Adobe RGB color gamuts "with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges." They cover 80 percent of the Rec.2020 gamut for HDR video editing and color grading, an impressive figure for a laptop display. The company also touts "cutting-edge factory calibration" to ensure luminance, white point and color gamut align with standard targets, making it useful for "filmmaking, design and even medical imaging," Apple claims. Its advanced display engine also controls each pixel's color and luminance "at the sub-millisecond level" to compensate for content, temperature and environment. That tech also addresses a key problem with OLED (organic pixel degradation over time), by adapting each pixel's age and usage. The new laptops use Apple's 120Hz ProMotion display for reasonably high refresh rates when gaming or creating content. And if you work outside at times or in a bright environment, you can get the new models with Apple's nano-texture option that's "now precisely etched into the cover glass," Apple says, to further reduce glare. The new MacBook Pros with PROLED XDR touch displays probably aren't worth the higher $400 base price for most people. With all the tech it's crammed into the displays, though, the models will be awfully tempting for users who make their money by creating content.

The company also touts "cutting-edge factory calibration" to ensure luminance, white point and color gamut align with standard targets, making it useful for "filmmaking, design and even medical imaging," Apple claims. Its advanced display engine also controls each pixel's color and luminance "at the sub-millisecond level" to compensate for content, temperature and environment. That tech also addresses a key problem with OLED (organic pixel degradation over time), by adapting each pixel's age and usage.

The new laptops use Apple's 120Hz ProMotion display for reasonably high refresh rates when gaming or creating content. And if you work outside at times or in a bright environment, you can get the new models with Apple's nano-texture option that's "now precisely etched into the cover glass," Apple says, to further reduce glare.

The new MacBook Pros with PROLED XDR touch displays probably aren't worth the higher $400 base price for most people. With all the tech it's crammed into the displays, though, the models will be awfully tempting for users who make their money by creating content.

extraction.body: The new MacBook Pro brings with it a bunch of firsts for Apple laptops, the two flashiest being an OLED display and touchscreen functionality. It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes. CMFs, or color-matching functions, mathematically represent how we perceive color, and there are a few different variations. We all have small discrepancies in our eyes — such as the sensitivity of the cones in our eyes, which allow us to see color — and those can change as we age. Apple CMF 2026 addresses that, so that displays look the same regardless of the technology they use. Apple first included its new CMF on the Studio Display XDR, which I reviewed earlier this year and found to be an excellent, albeit expensive, monitor for color professionals because of Apple CMF 2026 and the reference color modes. But the fact that this technology is now on a laptop that’s portable and not just a standalone monitor living on a desk is a big help for professionals on the move. As on the Studio Display XDR, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has two Apple CMF 2026 reference modes — one for P3 color primaries and one that includes both P3 and Adobe RGB color primaries for more flexibility. Peak brightness with both HDR and SDR content is 2,000 nits (on the XDR monitor peak SDR luminance is up to 1,000 nits), and the True Tone setting automatically adjusts HDR tone mapping, brightness, and white point based on ambient lighting. (An option to disable True Tone is in Displays preferences.) The MacBook doesn’t require using Apple CMF 2026, as there are 14 more reference color modes that use the CIE 1931 color space — it is still the standard, after all — including DICOM for medical imaging (which is cool, but only useful to those in the medical field). The MacBook also supports Apple Pro Display Calibrator, which includes three calibration methods to adjust the reference color modes, or a custom mode, if necessary. Color science and display technologies have come a long way since 1931, when the CIE 1931 color space was established. Apple’s development of the Apple CMF 2026 and its standardization efforts — the company is currently working with a CIE technical committee on a proposed standard — is an important step to make sure current display technologies look the same to as many people as possible.

extraction.body: We were dead wrong about Apple this time, and we couldn't be happier: Apple actually pulled it off , a 100% new, no-nonsense 13-inch MacBook for $600. Confirming lots of rumors ahead of its reveal, the MacBook Neo (starts at $599; $499 for education buyers) pairs Apple's A18 Pro processor (found in the iPhone 16 Pro of 2024) with 8GB of unified memory and up to 512GB of storage, all inside a slightly smaller MacBook chassis with fun new colors. The Neo isn't flawless (we'd tweak the laptop's ports, for one thing), but it takes many of the MacBook Air's strengths and squeezes them into a more affordable device for everyone, from students to straight-up-broke Mac fans. Poised to upend the budget-laptop market at a time everything else is just getting pricier, Apple's MacBook Neo earns an emphatic Editors' Choice award. Configurations: A Single, Simple Upgrade Option Starting at $599 ($499 for students), the MacBook Neo comes in a single configuration with just one upgrade option. Apple's MacBook Neo, Tested: This is 2026's Breakout Budget Laptop These are likely A18 Pro chips that were “binned” during iPhone chip manufacturing. Here, the Neo's A18 Pros could be chips with one GPU core that wasn't up to snuff. Apple’s A18 Pro is a mobile system-on-chip (SoC) that integrates graphics, memory, and other subsystem controllers. This SoC packaging means the laptop’s 8GB of unified memory is not upgradable—it’s baked in. Is it the Touch ID for security or the doubled-up storage that compels people to throw another $100 Apple’s way? Design: The Smallest (and Slightest) MacBook The MacBook Neo is basically a smaller, more colorful MacBook Air that’s lighter on features. Apple sells it in four colors: Indigo, Blush, Citrus, and silver; the first three you may know better as dark blue, pink, and a sort of lime yellow-green. Beyond the quirky three colors, color coding is a nifty perk here. The different color schemes carry through to the keyboard, the bottom cover’s rubber feet, and many macOS interface elements, such as scroll wheels and confirmation buttons—a bit of real, nifty polish. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) This new laptop is clearly inspired by the existing MacBook design launched back in 2022, but with a bunch of tweaks. The Neo is a little thicker than the 0.44-inch MacBook Air models, at exactly half an inch thick. Beyond this and the slightly smaller (13-inch) display, the Neo shows a few more subtle differences from Apple’s former budget laptop . I immediately noticed that the brushed finish on the Neo’s aluminum housing is more pronounced than on other MacBooks, possibly because it's made with a higher percentage of recycled materials (60%) than any Apple product to date. It’s a fuzzier, fun look. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) The Neo chassis also features side-firing speakers instead of speakers beneath the keyboard, venting out slits on the left and right side that resemble SD-card slots. As noted earlier, the keyboard lacks a Touch ID power button on the base model. Finally, the webcam, mounted above the screen, doesn't have the usual MacBook "notch" cutting down into the display area—instead, the screen bezels were made a bit thicker to accommodate the lens. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) How does this all compare with its budget PC competition? None of the PC laptops we benchmarked against the MacBook Neo has a full-metal frame, and only one might be as rigid and resistant to bending. That’s the Framework Laptop 12 , built to meet MIL-STD-810 durability requirements and clad in rubber bumpers. (It also starts at $200 more than the Neo and has a smaller screen.) Not one of these laptops is as thin or light as the MacBook Neo, either, generally by around a pound and a few tenths of an inch across the board. Meanwhile, the 12-inch Framework Laptop 12 is just a tenth of a pound heavier—the price of ruggedization. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) Finally, none of these competitors comes close to the MacBook Neo on screen quality. The Neo's display is sharper than any budget 13-inch laptop's, but not quite a 1440p panel, and it shines with more than 500 nits of brightness and broad coverage of the sRGB color gamut (borne out in our testing). I’ll dig more into the port arrangement, display, and other features, but the spoiler is that the Neo’s connectivity suite is its biggest disappointment. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) On the whole, though, the MacBook Neo is a brand-new Apple laptop that brings the usual MacBook standards for design and material quality to a remarkable new low price. You’ll likely hear or see a lot of reviews say, “Only Apple could do this,” when speaking of the MacBook Neo’s build quality and performance mix. That might be true, but if so, it’s the result of Apple’s deeply integrated positions in chip and device manufacturing, coupled with control of its entire product stack, and buoyed by its gargantuan cash reserves to weather any missteps or, ahem, supply chain upheavals. Display and Webcam: Well Ahead of Most Budget Laptops At first glance, the MacBook Neo’s 13-inch Liquid Retina screen doesn’t look much different from the MacBook Air’s, save for its smaller size. This IPS LED-backlit panel has a resolution of 2,408 by 1,506 pixels, which is sharper than most, if not any, budget 13-inch laptop display. While it's not quite 1440p, it's remarkable for a $599 laptop. By stripping away all of the supporting features it has built up on the MacBook Air and Pro laptops over the years, like support for high dynamic range (HDR), True Tone automated color adjustment, and nano-texture anti-reflective layers. I don’t think the MacBook Neo’s audience will miss them much—I don’t after using the laptop for a few days now. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) The screen shines at an impressive 516 nits in our tests, beating Apple’s own 500-nit claim, and refreshes at a standard 60Hz. The display’s only officially supported color gamut is sRGB, the standard for mainstream computers. Still, Apple’s Liquid Retina takes LED-backlit IPS to its logical conclusion, displaying up to 1 billion different colors through a panel with 10-bit color depth. A 10-bit color depth is rare on laptop displays at this price, generally reserved for laptops much closer to $1,000 and beyond. I measured 96% coverage of the sRGB spectrum in my testing. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) Finally, while you won’t see any nano-texture etching option for this display (that's reserved for models like the MacBook Pros), Apple says the MacBook Neo screen has an anti-reflective coating.

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple unveils groundbreaking MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch for the first time on Mac
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, 1 Live Activities, and Siri AI.
2 And with up to 24 hours of battery life in thinner and much lighter 3- and 4-pound designs, MacBook Pro is more portable than ever, empowering pros to take their work wherever inspiration strikes.
An enhanced six-speaker sound system now provides 50 percent deeper bass and remarkable sound clarity for even more immersive audio.
2 It is available to pre-order starting today, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.
“PROLED XDR is the world’s best laptop display.
It pairs state-of-the-art tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in our display engine to deliver the kind of visual fidelity pros have been dreaming of.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
PROLED XDR offers pros a super-wide color gamut with P3 and now Adobe RGB — critical for workflows in photography and design — along with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges.
2020 coverage for HDR video editing and color grading.
Cutting-edge factory calibration ensures luminance, white point, and color gamut are precisely aligned with standard targets.
Both color spaces are accessible within a single default preset, streamlining pro workflows and making it seamless to switch between them.
7 And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so apps perform at incredible speed.
The new MacBook Pro comes to life with macOS 27.

Siri AI can draw on personal context to help pros find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections.

Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence by using a dedicated keyboard shortcut to get help with a specific item.
Pros can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users.

Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display.
And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love.

In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 provide fast, reliable wireless connectivity, and Touch ID enables a quick, easy, and secure login experience.

With all the fuss about Apple finally releasing a touchscreen MacBook Pro , you may have forgotten about the new model's other key display technology: OLED, or what Apple calls PROLED XDR. It's typical of Apple to change a standard tech term to a cringy marketing-focused name, but in this case, the "PRO" designation appears to be justified. The new MacBook Pros are squarely aimed at photographers, artists and video editors who can justify the high price for a high-quality touch display. To appeal to those folks, Apple didn't just integrate a touch feature and OLED display and call it a day. Rather, it built what looks like one of the best pro laptop displays ever, with high brightness and contrast, excellent color accuracy and even a display engine that adapts to a pixel's age. For the new models, Apple used tandem OLED technology (first employed on the M4 iPad Pro) that stacks multiple organic layers into a single display panel. Judging by an Apple graphic in its press release, it appears to use a triangular pixel arrangement and not a striped RGB OLED system that can offer sharper text (we've reached out to the company for clarification on that). There are several key benefits to tandem OLED tech, namely high peak HDR brightness, a lower burn-in risk and a longer panel lifespan. It's also brighter and more color-accurate when viewed from an angle. At the same time, it retains and even improves the primary benefit of OLED displays: extremely high contrast. Apple says that the new MacBook Pros with PROLED XDR deliver up to 2,000 nits peak HDR, compared to 1,600 nits peak HDR for current models with Mini LED tech. That's very high for an OLED display and at least as bright or brighter than any other OLED laptop on the market (if accurate). Apple also touts an "industry-leading" 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, much higher than current MacBook Pro models. The PROLED XDR screens also offer high color accuracy. Apple says the new models now cover both the P3 (HDR) and Adobe RGB color gamuts "with notably wider coverage in green and cyan ranges." They cover 80 percent of the Rec.2020 gamut for HDR video editing and color grading, an impressive figure for a laptop display. The company also touts "cutting-edge factory calibration" to ensure luminance, white point and color gamut align with standard targets, making it useful for "filmmaking, design and even medical imaging," Apple claims. Its advanced display engine also controls each pixel's color and luminance "at the sub-millisecond level" to compensate for content, temperature and environment. That tech also addresses a key problem with OLED (organic pixel degradation over time), by adapting each pixel's age and usage. The new laptops use Apple's 120Hz ProMotion display for reasonably high refresh rates when gaming or creating content. And if you work outside at times or in a bright environment, you can get the new models with Apple's nano-texture option that's "now precisely etched into the cover glass," Apple says, to further reduce glare. The new MacBook Pros with PROLED XDR touch displays probably aren't worth the higher $400 base price for most people. With all the tech it's crammed into the displays, though, the models will be awfully tempting for users who make their money by creating content.

extraction.body: The new MacBook Pro brings with it a bunch of firsts for Apple laptops, the two flashiest being an OLED display and touchscreen functionality. It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes. CMFs, or color-matching functions, mathematically represent how we perceive color, and there are a few different variations. We all have small discrepancies in our eyes — such as the sensitivity of the cones in our eyes, which allow us to see color — and those can change as we age. Apple CMF 2026 addresses that, so that displays look the same regardless of the technology they use. Apple first included its new CMF on the Studio Display XDR, which I reviewed earlier this year and found to be an excellent, albeit expensive, monitor for color professionals because of Apple CMF 2026 and the reference color modes. But the fact that this technology is now on a laptop that’s portable and not just a standalone monitor living on a desk is a big help for professionals on the move. As on the Studio Display XDR, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has two Apple CMF 2026 reference modes — one for P3 color primaries and one that includes both P3 and Adobe RGB color primaries for more flexibility. Peak brightness with both HDR and SDR content is 2,000 nits (on the XDR monitor peak SDR luminance is up to 1,000 nits), and the True Tone setting automatically adjusts HDR tone mapping, brightness, and white point based on ambient lighting. (An option to disable True Tone is in Displays preferences.) The MacBook doesn’t require using Apple CMF 2026, as there are 14 more reference color modes that use the CIE 1931 color space — it is still the standard, after all — including DICOM for medical imaging (which is cool, but only useful to those in the medical field). The MacBook also supports Apple Pro Display Calibrator, which includes three calibration methods to adjust the reference color modes, or a custom mode, if necessary. Color science and display technologies have come a long way since 1931, when the CIE 1931 color space was established. Apple’s development of the Apple CMF 2026 and its standardization efforts — the company is currently working with a CIE technical committee on a proposed standard — is an important step to make sure current display technologies look the same to as many people as possible.

extraction.body: We were dead wrong about Apple this time, and we couldn't be happier: Apple actually pulled it off , a 100% new, no-nonsense 13-inch MacBook for $600. Confirming lots of rumors ahead of its reveal, the MacBook Neo (starts at $599; $499 for education buyers) pairs Apple's A18 Pro processor (found in the iPhone 16 Pro of 2024) with 8GB of unified memory and up to 512GB of storage, all inside a slightly smaller MacBook chassis with fun new colors. The Neo isn't flawless (we'd tweak the laptop's ports, for one thing), but it takes many of the MacBook Air's strengths and squeezes them into a more affordable device for everyone, from students to straight-up-broke Mac fans. Poised to upend the budget-laptop market at a time everything else is just getting pricier, Apple's MacBook Neo earns an emphatic Editors' Choice award. Configurations: A Single, Simple Upgrade Option Starting at $599 ($499 for students), the MacBook Neo comes in a single configuration with just one upgrade option. Apple's MacBook Neo, Tested: This is 2026's Breakout Budget Laptop These are likely A18 Pro chips that were “binned” during iPhone chip manufacturing. Here, the Neo's A18 Pros could be chips with one GPU core that wasn't up to snuff. Apple’s A18 Pro is a mobile system-on-chip (SoC) that integrates graphics, memory, and other subsystem controllers. This SoC packaging means the laptop’s 8GB of unified memory is not upgradable—it’s baked in. Is it the Touch ID for security or the doubled-up storage that compels people to throw another $100 Apple’s way? Design: The Smallest (and Slightest) MacBook The MacBook Neo is basically a smaller, more colorful MacBook Air that’s lighter on features. Apple sells it in four colors: Indigo, Blush, Citrus, and silver; the first three you may know better as dark blue, pink, and a sort of lime yellow-green. Beyond the quirky three colors, color coding is a nifty perk here. The different color schemes carry through to the keyboard, the bottom cover’s rubber feet, and many macOS interface elements, such as scroll wheels and confirmation buttons—a bit of real, nifty polish. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) This new laptop is clearly inspired by the existing MacBook design launched back in 2022, but with a bunch of tweaks. The Neo is a little thicker than the 0.44-inch MacBook Air models, at exactly half an inch thick. Beyond this and the slightly smaller (13-inch) display, the Neo shows a few more subtle differences from Apple’s former budget laptop . I immediately noticed that the brushed finish on the Neo’s aluminum housing is more pronounced than on other MacBooks, possibly because it's made with a higher percentage of recycled materials (60%) than any Apple product to date. It’s a fuzzier, fun look. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) The Neo chassis also features side-firing speakers instead of speakers beneath the keyboard, venting out slits on the left and right side that resemble SD-card slots. As noted earlier, the keyboard lacks a Touch ID power button on the base model. Finally, the webcam, mounted above the screen, doesn't have the usual MacBook "notch" cutting down into the display area—instead, the screen bezels were made a bit thicker to accommodate the lens. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) How does this all compare with its budget PC competition? None of the PC laptops we benchmarked against the MacBook Neo has a full-metal frame, and only one might be as rigid and resistant to bending. That’s the Framework Laptop 12 , built to meet MIL-STD-810 durability requirements and clad in rubber bumpers. (It also starts at $200 more than the Neo and has a smaller screen.) Not one of these laptops is as thin or light as the MacBook Neo, either, generally by around a pound and a few tenths of an inch across the board. Meanwhile, the 12-inch Framework Laptop 12 is just a tenth of a pound heavier—the price of ruggedization. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) Finally, none of these competitors comes close to the MacBook Neo on screen quality. The Neo's display is sharper than any budget 13-inch laptop's, but not quite a 1440p panel, and it shines with more than 500 nits of brightness and broad coverage of the sRGB color gamut (borne out in our testing). I’ll dig more into the port arrangement, display, and other features, but the spoiler is that the Neo’s connectivity suite is its biggest disappointment. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) On the whole, though, the MacBook Neo is a brand-new Apple laptop that brings the usual MacBook standards for design and material quality to a remarkable new low price. You’ll likely hear or see a lot of reviews say, “Only Apple could do this,” when speaking of the MacBook Neo’s build quality and performance mix. That might be true, but if so, it’s the result of Apple’s deeply integrated positions in chip and device manufacturing, coupled with control of its entire product stack, and buoyed by its gargantuan cash reserves to weather any missteps or, ahem, supply chain upheavals. Display and Webcam: Well Ahead of Most Budget Laptops At first glance, the MacBook Neo’s 13-inch Liquid Retina screen doesn’t look much different from the MacBook Air’s, save for its smaller size. This IPS LED-backlit panel has a resolution of 2,408 by 1,506 pixels, which is sharper than most, if not any, budget 13-inch laptop display. While it's not quite 1440p, it's remarkable for a $599 laptop. By stripping away all of the supporting features it has built up on the MacBook Air and Pro laptops over the years, like support for high dynamic range (HDR), True Tone automated color adjustment, and nano-texture anti-reflective layers. I don’t think the MacBook Neo’s audience will miss them much—I don’t after using the laptop for a few days now. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) The screen shines at an impressive 516 nits in our tests, beating Apple’s own 500-nit claim, and refreshes at a standard 60Hz. The display’s only officially supported color gamut is sRGB, the standard for mainstream computers. Still, Apple’s Liquid Retina takes LED-backlit IPS to its logical conclusion, displaying up to 1 billion different colors through a panel with 10-bit color depth. A 10-bit color depth is rare on laptop displays at this price, generally reserved for laptops much closer to $1,000 and beyond. I measured 96% coverage of the sRGB spectrum in my testing. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) Finally, while you won’t see any nano-texture etching option for this display (that's reserved for models like the MacBook Pros), Apple says the MacBook Neo screen has an anti-reflective coating.

Design: The Smallest (and Slightest) MacBook The MacBook Neo is basically a smaller, more colorful MacBook Air that’s lighter on features.
Apple sells it in four colors: Indigo, Blush, Citrus, and silver; the first three you may know better as dark blue, pink, and a sort of lime yellow-green.
Beyond the quirky three colors, color coding is a nifty perk here.

The different color schemes carry through to the keyboard, the bottom cover’s rubber feet, and many macOS interface elements, such as scroll wheels and confirmation buttons—a bit of real, nifty polish. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) This new laptop is clearly inspired by the existing MacBook design launched back in 2022, but with a bunch of tweaks.
The Neo is a little thicker than the 0.44-inch MacBook Air models, at exactly half an inch thick.
Beyond this and the slightly smaller (13-inch) display, the Neo shows a few more subtle differences from Apple’s former budget laptop .

I immediately noticed that the brushed finish on the Neo’s aluminum housing is more pronounced than on other MacBooks, possibly because it's made with a higher percentage of recycled materials (60%) than any Apple product to date.

It’s a fuzzier, fun look. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) The Neo chassis also features side-firing speakers instead of speakers beneath the keyboard, venting out slits on the left and right side that resemble SD-card slots.
As noted earlier, the keyboard lacks a Touch ID power button on the base model.

Finally, the webcam, mounted above the screen, doesn't have the usual MacBook "notch" cutting down into the display area—instead, the screen bezels were made a bit thicker to accommodate the lens. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) How does this all compare with its budget PC competition?
None of the PC laptops we benchmarked against the MacBook Neo has a full-metal frame, and only one might be as rigid and resistant to bending.

That’s the Framework Laptop 12 , built to meet MIL-STD-810 durability requirements and clad in rubber bumpers. (It also starts at $200 more than the Neo and has a smaller screen.) Not one of these laptops is as thin or light as the MacBook Neo, either, generally by around a pound and a few tenths of an inch across the board.

Meanwhile, the 12-inch Framework Laptop 12 is just a tenth of a pound heavier—the price of ruggedization. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) Finally, none of these competitors comes close to the MacBook Neo on screen quality.

The Neo's display is sharper than any budget 13-inch laptop's, but not quite a 1440p panel, and it shines with more than 500 nits of brightness and broad coverage of the sRGB color gamut (borne out in our testing).

I’ll dig more into the port arrangement, display, and other features, but the spoiler is that the Neo’s connectivity suite is its biggest disappointment. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) On the whole, though, the MacBook Neo is a brand-new Apple laptop that brings the usual MacBook standards for design and material quality to a remarkable new low price.
You’ll likely hear or see a lot of reviews say, “Only Apple could do this,” when speaking of the MacBook Neo’s build quality and performance mix.

That might be true, but if so, it’s the result of Apple’s deeply integrated positions in chip and device manufacturing, coupled with control of its entire product stack, and buoyed by its gargantuan cash reserves to weather any missteps or, ahem, supply chain upheavals.
Display and Webcam: Well Ahead of Most Budget Laptops At first glance, the MacBook Neo’s 13-inch Liquid Retina screen doesn’t look much different from the MacBook Air’s, save for its smaller size.
This IPS LED-backlit panel has a resolution of 2,408 by 1,506 pixels, which is sharper than most, if not any, budget 13-inch laptop display.
While it's not quite 1440p, it's remarkable for a $599 laptop.

By stripping away all of the supporting features it has built up on the MacBook Air and Pro laptops over the years, like support for high dynamic range (HDR), True Tone automated color adjustment, and nano-texture anti-reflective layers.

I don’t think the MacBook Neo’s audience will miss them much—I don’t after using the laptop for a few days now. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) The screen shines at an impressive 516 nits in our tests, beating Apple’s own 500-nit claim, and refreshes at a standard 60Hz.
The display’s only officially supported color gamut is sRGB, the standard for mainstream computers.
Still, Apple’s Liquid Retina takes LED-backlit IPS to its logical conclusion, displaying up to 1 billion different colors through a panel with 10-bit color depth.
A 10-bit color depth is rare on laptop displays at this price, generally reserved for laptops much closer to $1,000 and beyond.

I measured 96% coverage of the sRGB spectrum in my testing. (Credit: Joseph Maldonado) Finally, while you won’t see any nano-texture etching option for this display (that's reserved for models like the MacBook Pros), Apple says the MacBook Neo screen has an anti-reflective coating.

sources.title: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks - CNBC
passages: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to the "shift to AI mode and AI overviews." The traffic decline played a big role in Reddit's planned efforts to require people to become logged-in users.

A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic .
Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.
"We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem.

And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.
The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance.

"I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said.

Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership.
Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million.
Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.

Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users , because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads.
It's an evolution of how these platforms work."

extraction.body: Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet." The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released. Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to the "shift to AI mode and AI overviews." The traffic decline played a big role in Reddit's planned efforts to require people to become logged-in users. A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic . "I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said. Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now." The CEO didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity . The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S. He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing. Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million. Huffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter. He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said. Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users , because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads. "The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said. The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings. Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion. "It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals." Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting. The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google. Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership. "I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said. Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet." "Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work." Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said. He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.

Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.
Huffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter.
He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said.

Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users , because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads.
"The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said.

The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings.
Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion.
"It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals."
Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.

The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.

Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership.
"I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said.
Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet."

"Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."

Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.

Reddit will no longer allow logged out users or those without an account to view content on its platform, CEO Steve Huffman shared in an update . The change, which the company said will initially be tested in "select markets" outside the US, comes as the company says that search traffic has declined significantly. "A key piece of work to retain new audiences is shifting Reddit to a logged-in-only experience," Huffman wrote in a shareholder letter. "Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them." The change is the most dramatic shift the company has made as it battles AI scraping and changes to internet search. It will also likely rattle users, some of whom are already frustrated with recent moves like restrictions on Old Reddit . Huffman said that it was a "big change" but necessary for the company. "It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally," he wrote. "It also allows us to protect access to Reddit's extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world." Huffman didn't explicitly mention age verification laws, but requiring users to log in would presumably help the company comply with such measures. Huffman said the company is still working on figuring out exactly when logged out users will encounter a "hard prompt" to log in. "We need to find the right boundary," he said during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "Whether they're coming from a shared link or maybe from search ... there'll be some version of Reddit accessible for those moments before we do that hard prompt." Reddit's CEO, who has been clearly frustrated with the state of online search and Google's AI overviews for a while, was more explicit in his criticism. "The reality is, the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody, as far as I know," he said. "So that's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it's not." The company reported that search traffic was "down meaningfully" in the most recent quarter, with the company seeing referrals from search drop by more than 1 million each week during the month of October. Reddit's relationship with Google is also complicated. The company has a licensing deal with the search giant so it can access the platform's data for AI training. That deal is reportedly worth about $60 million a year. More recently, there are reports that Reddit may be reconsidering this arrangement. When asked about it on the call, Huffman said there are "active discussions" but didn't share specifics. "What's most important is that any deal we do needs to advance our long-term strategy, it has to be a fair exchange of value," he said. Huffman hinted at some other product changes the company is considering to help it grow engagement with logged in users. The Reddit founder said the company is working on adding "more organization" to its main feed to make it "more consistent" and "less grab bag-ey" than it currently is. He also suggested that an "incognito mode" could be in the works. He speculated that adding "private browsing" could help the company address users who repeatedly uninstall and reinstall the Reddit app.

extraction.body: The company is starting with tests outside of the US. Reddit will no longer allow logged out users or those without an account to view content on its platform, CEO Steve Huffman shared in an update . The change, which the company said will initially be tested in "select markets" outside the US, comes as the company says that search traffic has declined significantly. "A key piece of work to retain new audiences is shifting Reddit to a logged-in-only experience," Huffman wrote in a shareholder letter. "Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them." The change is the most dramatic shift the company has made as it battles AI scraping and changes to internet search. It will also likely rattle users, some of whom are already frustrated with recent moves like restrictions on Old Reddit . Huffman said that it was a "big change" but necessary for the company. "It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally," he wrote. "It also allows us to protect access to Reddit's extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world." Huffman didn't explicitly mention age verification laws, but requiring users to log in would presumably help the company comply with such measures. Huffman said the company is still working on figuring out exactly when logged out users will encounter a "hard prompt" to log in. "We need to find the right boundary," he said during the company's third-quarter earnings call. "Whether they're coming from a shared link or maybe from search ... there'll be some version of Reddit accessible for those moments before we do that hard prompt." Reddit's CEO, who has been clearly frustrated with the state of online search and Google's AI overviews for a while, was more explicit in his criticism. "The reality is, the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody, as far as I know," he said. "So that's just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it's not." The company reported that search traffic was "down meaningfully" in the most recent quarter, with the company seeing referrals from search drop by more than 1 million each week during the month of October. Reddit's relationship with Google is also complicated. The company has a licensing deal with the search giant so it can access the platform's data for AI training. That deal is reportedly worth about $60 million a year. More recently, there are reports that Reddit may be reconsidering this arrangement. When asked about it on the call, Huffman said there are "active discussions" but didn't share specifics. "What's most important is that any deal we do needs to advance our long-term strategy, it has to be a fair exchange of value," he said. Huffman hinted at some other product changes the company is considering to help it grow engagement with logged in users. The Reddit founder said the company is working on adding "more organization" to its main feed to make it "more consistent" and "less grab bag-ey" than it currently is. He also suggested that an "incognito mode" could be in the works. He speculated that adding "private browsing" could help the company address users who repeatedly uninstall and reinstall the Reddit app.

extraction.body: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said in an earnings call today that Google’s AI-powered search modes do not help with traffic to the platform, echoing problems facing other websites and publishers. As part of its Q3 2026 earnings, Reddit revealed that search traffic in October has “dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week,” and he attributes part of the company’s struggles with Google traffic to how AI Mode and AI Overviews change the search experience. “The reality is, AI Mode does not drive traffic,” Huffman says. That’s just a fundamental shift in how Google works. It used to be a traffic driver, now it’s not.” He says that AI Overviews and AI Mode have “evolved a lot” and now, at a “minimum,” push “everyone down the search page.” Huffman also says that Reddit believes its content that’s machine-translated into other languages is being ranked lower in search results, which he says would primarily affect the company outside the US. However, Reddit is still a “top search term in Google,” Huffman says. “This doesn’t say anything about the internet consumers’ demand for Reddit. It says Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to.” He also says that Google is “crawling us as hard as ever, so the demand hasn’t changed from their point of view, either.” (Google’s business has been affected by AI Mode, too: it said yesterday that it’s seeing “lower monetization” in AI Mode ads, though it’s now bringing AI ads to more countries.) To try and combat the search referral difficulties, Reddit is working to make the platform a “direct, sticky, daily destination.” Yesterday, it introduced a “For You” feed with recommendations related to your interests, and in August, it started testing an experiment that uses AI to turn posts into short videos. Reddit also announced today that it’s going to force everyone to log in, which Huffman claims will be “better for user experience, better for our ads business, is more in line with safety regulations, and more protective of Reddit data.”

sources.title: Google rolls out new Gemini capabilities to Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive - TechCrunch
passages: Google announced on Tuesday that it’s bringing a slew of new Gemini-powered AI capabilities to Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive.
All the new features are rolling out today in beta and will first be available to Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers.
As for Sheets, Gemini is evolving from a tool you work in to a collaborative partner, Google says.
With a single prompt, it will pull relevant data from across your Gmail, Chat, and Drive to quickly create a fully formatted spreadsheet.

A new “Help me create” tool in Docs lets users describe what they want to create, and Gemini will follow their instructions and gather information from Drive, Gmail, and Chat to generate a first draft.
For example, you can ask Gemini to “draft a newsletter for our neighborhood association using the meeting minutes from my January HOA meeting and the list of upcoming events.”
Now, when you search in Drive using natural language, Gemini will surface an “AI Overview” at the top of your results, like the ones you see on Google Search.
The overview summarizes the most relevant information from your files, while citing its sources, so you don’t need to open a document to find what you’re looking for.
Docs is also getting a new “Match the format” tool that lets you mirror the structure and style of another document.
For more complex tasks, you can now use a “Fill with Gemini” tool to populate tables even faster.
The feature can instantly generate custom text, categorize and summarize data, or pull in real-time information from Google Search.
Gemini will suggest edits to make the tone and voice consistent throughout the draft.

extraction.body: Google announced on Tuesday that it’s bringing a slew of new Gemini-powered AI capabilities to Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive. The new features let users do things like quickly generate fully formatted first drafts, slides, and sheets based on information from their Gmail, Chat, and Drive. The tools are designed to make the apps more personal and capable of helping users get things done faster, right within the platforms themselves, instead of needing to switch to a separate tool or chatbot. A new “Help me create” tool in Docs lets users describe what they want to create, and Gemini will follow their instructions and gather information from Drive, Gmail, and Chat to generate a first draft. For example, you can ask Gemini to “draft a newsletter for our neighborhood association using the meeting minutes from my January HOA meeting and the list of upcoming events.” Once you have a first draft, Gemini can help refine specific sections without regenerating the entire document. You can also use the “Help me write” tool to do things like improve clarity or add details where needed. Additionally, if you have multiple people working on a draft with differing voices and tones, you can now use a new “Match writing style” feature to help unify the documents. Gemini will suggest edits to make the tone and voice consistent throughout the draft. Docs is also getting a new “Match the format” tool that lets you mirror the structure and style of another document. For example, if you find a travel itinerary template you like, Gemini can fill it in with your own trip details by pulling information from your emails, such as flight confirmations, hotel bookings, and rental car reservations. As for Sheets, Gemini is evolving from a tool you work in to a collaborative partner, Google says. With a single prompt, it will pull relevant data from across your Gmail, Chat, and Drive to quickly create a fully formatted spreadsheet. For example, you could ask it to “ organize my upcoming move to Chicago. Create a checklist for packing by room, a contact list for utilities, and a spreadsheet to track moving company quotes from my inbox.” For more complex tasks, you can now use a “Fill with Gemini” tool to populate tables even faster. The feature can instantly generate custom text, categorize and summarize data, or pull in real-time information from Google Search. For instance, if you’re managing your college applications, you might have a tracker for all your application details. Instead of manually looking up each school’s deadlines, tuition, and other information, you can set up column headers for the details you need, then let Gemini fill in the table automatically by pulling relevant information from the web. Over on Sheets, you can now have Gemini generate a fully editable slide in your deck that matches your overall theme, drawing on context from your files, emails, and the web. If you don’t like a slide, you can ask Gemini to adjust it by asking it to do things like “match the colors to the rest of my deck” or “make this more minimal.” In the future, Google says Slides will let you create a complete presentation from a single prompt, using relevant context when needed. For instance, you will be able to ask Gemini to “create a 5-slide deck for my upcoming Tokyo trip.” Google also announced that it’s making Drive no longer just a place to store your files, but more of an active collaborator. Now, when you search in Drive using natural language, Gemini will surface an “AI Overview” at the top of your results, like the ones you see on Google Search. The overview summarizes the most relevant information from your files, while citing its sources, so you don’t need to open a document to find what you’re looking for. A new “Ask Gemini in Drive” feature lets you ask complex questions across your documents, emails, calendar, and the web. For example, you could select all of your tax-related files and ask, “What should I ask my tax advisor before filing this year’s taxes?” and get a detailed answer based on your actual data. All the new features are rolling out today in beta and will first be available to Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers. They’re available in English worldwide for Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and in the U.S. for Drive. Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. extraction.body: Google announced on Tuesday that it’s bringing a slew of new Gemini-powered AI capabilities to Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive. The new features let users do things like quickly generate fully formatted first drafts, slides, and sheets based on information from their Gmail, Chat, and Drive. The tools are designed to make the apps more personal and capable of helping users get things done faster, right within the platforms themselves, instead of needing to switch to a separate tool or chatbot. A new “Help me create” tool in Docs lets users describe what they want to create, and Gemini will follow their instructions and gather information from Drive, Gmail, and Chat to generate a first draft. For example, you can ask Gemini to “draft a newsletter for our neighborhood association using the meeting minutes from my January HOA meeting and the list of upcoming events.” Once you have a first draft, Gemini can help refine specific sections without regenerating the entire document. You can also use the “Help me write” tool to do things like improve clarity or add details where needed. Additionally, if you have multiple people working on a draft with differing voices and tones, you can now use a new “Match writing style” feature to help unify the documents. Gemini will suggest edits to make the tone and voice consistent throughout the draft. Docs is also getting a new “Match the format” tool that lets you mirror the structure and style of another document. For example, if you find a travel itinerary template you like, Gemini can fill it in with your own trip details by pulling information from your emails, such as flight confirmations, hotel bookings, and rental car reservations. As for Sheets, Gemini is evolving from a tool you work in to a collaborative partner, Google says. With a single prompt, it will pull relevant data from across your Gmail, Chat, and Drive to quickly create a fully formatted spreadsheet. For example, you could ask it to “ organize my upcoming move to Chicago. Create a checklist for packing by room, a contact list for utilities, and a spreadsheet to track moving company quotes from my inbox.” For more complex tasks, you can now use a “Fill with Gemini” tool to populate tables even faster. The feature can instantly generate custom text, categorize and summarize data, or pull in real-time information from Google Search. For instance, if you’re managing your college applications, you might have a tracker for all your application details. Instead of manually looking up each school’s deadlines, tuition, and other information, you can set up column headers for the details you need, then let Gemini fill in the table automatically by pulling relevant information from the web. Over on Sheets, you can now have Gemini generate a fully editable slide in your deck that matches your overall theme, drawing on context from your files, emails, and the web. If you don’t like a slide, you can ask Gemini to adjust it by asking it to do things like “match the colors to the rest of my deck” or “make this more minimal.” In the future, Google says Slides will let you create a complete presentation from a single prompt, using relevant context when needed. For instance, you will be able to ask Gemini to “create a 5-slide deck for my upcoming Tokyo trip.” Google also announced that it’s making Drive no longer just a place to store your files, but more of an active collaborator. Now, when you search in Drive using natural language, Gemini will surface an “AI Overview” at the top of your results, like the ones you see on Google Search. The overview summarizes the most relevant information from your files, while citing its sources, so you don’t need to open a document to find what you’re looking for. A new “Ask Gemini in Drive” feature lets you ask complex questions across your documents, emails, calendar, and the web. For example, you could select all of your tax-related files and ask, “What should I ask my tax advisor before filing this year’s taxes?” and get a detailed answer based on your actual data. All the new features are rolling out today in beta and will first be available to Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers. They’re available in English worldwide for Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and in the U.S. for Drive. Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. relevantPassages.text: Google announced on Tuesday that it’s bringing a slew of new Gemini-powered AI capabilities to Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive.
All the new features are rolling out today in beta and will first be available to Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers.
As for Sheets, Gemini is evolving from a tool you work in to a collaborative partner, Google says.
With a single prompt, it will pull relevant data from across your Gmail, Chat, and Drive to quickly create a fully formatted spreadsheet.

A new “Help me create” tool in Docs lets users describe what they want to create, and Gemini will follow their instructions and gather information from Drive, Gmail, and Chat to generate a first draft.
For example, you can ask Gemini to “draft a newsletter for our neighborhood association using the meeting minutes from my January HOA meeting and the list of upcoming events.”
Now, when you search in Drive using natural language, Gemini will surface an “AI Overview” at the top of your results, like the ones you see on Google Search.
The overview summarizes the most relevant information from your files, while citing its sources, so you don’t need to open a document to find what you’re looking for.
Docs is also getting a new “Match the format” tool that lets you mirror the structure and style of another document.
For more complex tasks, you can now use a “Fill with Gemini” tool to populate tables even faster.
The feature can instantly generate custom text, categorize and summarize data, or pull in real-time information from Google Search.
Gemini will suggest edits to make the tone and voice consistent throughout the draft.

sources.title: I tried Apple's new touchscreen MacBook Pro, and touching a MacBook screen feels wonderfully natural - TechRadar
passages: Confirming one of Apple 's worst-kept secrets, Apple finally unveiled its first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro in 14-inch and 16-inch models on Wednesday, October 28, in Los Angeles.
The news comes just days after Apple unveiled M6-class MacBook Pros .
Notably, the new PROLED touchscreen laptops are running M5 Pro and M5 Max Apple silicon.
Yes, I found myself touching the inert MacBook screen and had to retrain myself to stop doing it.
If you read no further, know this: it felt totally natural to tap, swipe, gesture with three fingers, pinch, zoom, and more on a MacBook Pro display.
It lights up when you open the laptop and turns off when you close it (people at the Hollywood, California, event were cheering for that).
Honestly, if it can't fold back at least flat, there's no point in this support anyway.
Pre-orders are live today, and the laptops ship on November 6.
At no moment did I hesitate and wonder how I did this or that thing.
It never felt uncomfortable, and my arm never got tired.
Put another way, a touchscreen is a perfect fit for the MacBook Pro family,
As a former Windows user, and more specifically a longtime Surface Pro fan, I'm actually quite used to touching a screen, though maybe not one quite as beautiful as this.
For those unfamiliar with tandem OLED technology, which Apple first introduced a few years ago with the iPad Pro, it sandwiches two ultra-thin, light-emitting OLEDs together.
This increases the brightness while maintaining incredibly inky blacks (they're gorgeous).
It also allows for a far thinner display panel because you don't need a backlight.
