sources.title: Binance hack: Tether, Circle freeze $2.4 billion in crypto assets; Bitcoin tumbles below $79,000 | Here's what happened
passages: Zhao said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.How much crypto was frozen?The two largest stablecoin issuers, Tether and Circle, also moved to freeze digital assets linked to the suspected incident.Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino said his company had frozen more than $1.5 billion in USDT “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”.Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said $800 million of its USDC had been frozen amid reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.USDT and USDC are stablecoins whose value is pegged to the US dollar.Meanwhile, blockchain tracker Arkham identified wallets associated with the suspected hacker holding about $5.9 billion in digital assets.

However, this figure does not necessarily represent the amount stolen from Binance.How did Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies react?Bitcoin slumped as much as 3.7%, falling below $79,000 to its lowest level since September, as news of the suspected hack weighed on investor sentiment.

Other digital tokens also sold off.“The rumoured Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data, told Bloomberg.“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole,” he added.The sell-off comes after a two-month-long price rebound in the cryptocurrency market.

It said it was working to restore services when it was safe to do so.However, several industry experts said the incident appeared to involve a significant amount of stolen assets.“It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company but remains its largest shareholder.

The fund is generally maintained at around $1 billion.“Hot wallets getting drained is not something new to crypto, but the amount would be a meaningful hack on the largest crypto exchange,” said James Seyffart of Bloomberg Intelligence.“It's definitely a bad look.

The incident was attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea.Binance has an emergency reserve fund, the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), established in 2018 to protect customers in extreme situations.

extraction.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by daily trading volumes, is investigating a suspected major hack after freezing more than $2.5 billion in digital assets, triggering a sell-off across cryptocurrency markets.The exchange said it had frozen $2.54 billion in assets and could raise that figure further as its teams work with law enforcement, stablecoin issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners.Binance said it had not confirmed any impact on customer funds. “At this stage, we have not confirmed any impact to user funds,” a company spokesperson said, adding that its security teams were investigating reports of a potential security issue.The exchange also suspended withdrawals on multiple networks, describing the move as a precautionary measure. It said it was working to restore services when it was safe to do so.However, several industry experts said the incident appeared to involve a significant amount of stolen assets.“It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company but remains its largest shareholder. Zhao said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.How much crypto was frozen?The two largest stablecoin issuers, Tether and Circle, also moved to freeze digital assets linked to the suspected incident.Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino said his company had frozen more than $1.5 billion in USDT “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”.Circle chief Jeremy Allaire said $800 million of its USDC had been frozen amid reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.USDT and USDC are stablecoins whose value is pegged to the US dollar.Meanwhile, blockchain tracker Arkham identified wallets associated with the suspected hacker holding about $5.9 billion in digital assets. However, this figure does not necessarily represent the amount stolen from Binance.How did Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies react?Bitcoin slumped as much as 3.7%, falling below $79,000 to its lowest level since September, as news of the suspected hack weighed on investor sentiment. Other digital tokens also sold off.“The rumoured Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data, told Bloomberg.“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole,” he added.The sell-off comes after a two-month-long price rebound in the cryptocurrency market. Traders were already preparing for volatility, with $11 billion in crypto options scheduled to expire on Friday.Why is Binance hack significant?If confirmed, the incident could surpass the February 2025 attack on crypto exchange Bybit, in which hackers stole almost $1.5 billion in tokens. The incident was attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea.Binance has an emergency reserve fund, the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), established in 2018 to protect customers in extreme situations. The fund is generally maintained at around $1 billion.“Hot wallets getting drained is not something new to crypto, but the amount would be a meaningful hack on the largest crypto exchange,” said James Seyffart of Bloomberg Intelligence.“It's definitely a bad look. And this is one after another,” he added, referring to a recent spate of security incidents.The Binance incident also came on the same day that Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after a third-party software provider was compromised. Blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps said that more than 700 users had lost $2.7 million.(With inputs from agencies)

sources.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
passages: Google is still making a huge amount of money, but there are several troubling trends emerging.
The last few years at the company have been all about AI, with generative technology appearing in products from Gmail to Android.
Most notably, Google is shifting to an AI search platform powered by Gemini models.
Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September.
But the company’s stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history.
In the last quarter, Google saw search grow by 12 percent versus last year.
Except that’s a much slower rate than previous quarters.
Growth in Q2 was 17 percent, and Q1 saw 19 percent growth over 2025.
So that’s the first problem, likely driven by more consumers using AI chatbots to find answers.
The other issue is that Google’s take on AI search isn’t pulling in revenue like standard web search yet.
According to Schindler, each AI Mode query earns less revenue compared to a similar web search—there are fewer ads, and they cost less to run.
Google is not slowing down—it’s only going to accelerate the shift toward more AI.
The loss actually increased from -$5.8 billion to -$9.06 billion, a situation that is directly attributable to Google’s runaway AI spending.
Google had capital expenditures of $51.4 billion in Q3 and says it still expects total 2026 spending to be between $195 billion and $205 billion.
In 2027, Google is targeting more than $300 billion of AI investment.
While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more.
Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02.
That’s about a billion more than analyst guesses.
As part of the financial disclosure, Google announced an expansion of ads in AI Mode.
If you do decide to dip into Google’s search chatbot, you’ll probably see more contextual advertising.
These ads will begin appearing in more international markets soon.
In the US, where AI Mode ads were already becoming commonplace, Google will implement multi-turn ads.
That means the sponsored links will change continuously as you engage in a back-and-forth with the robot.
CEO Sundar Pichai noted that these complex interactions are becoming more common as Google pushes more users toward AI Mode.
To support this continued spending, Google points to its cloud revenue more than doubling over the past year.
It’s easy to see why the company is so keen to keep expanding in AI based on that.
Countless AI startups pay to run models on Google’s infrastructure.
But even the larger AI firms are using venture cash to do it, and if that funding were to dry up, Google’s cloud revenues could go with it.
While Google’s investments ensure it still turns a profit, the trend of spending more than it earns on products and services (that negative cash flow) could come back to bite it.
Search growth is declining, and Google is placing all its eggs in the AI basket.

extraction.body: Google told investors on October 28, 2026 that AI Mode queries earn less money than comparable traditional Search queries, and the company says more ads are the answer, Ars Technica reported . The admission came on Alphabet’s Q3 2026 earnings call. It matters because Google Search remains the cash engine behind everything else the company builds, including the Gemini models that power its newest search products. Philipp Schindler, Google’s chief business officer and a senior vice president, framed the issue in plain terms. Fast growth in AI Mode queries dragged on revenue growth because each of those queries monetizes at a lower rate today. Google Search and other advertising revenue still hit roughly $63.3 billion, up 12% year over year, but the mix is shifting toward a format that pays less per question. This article breaks down what Google actually confirmed, what it left vague, how the company plans to close the gap with more Google AI Mode ads, and what the shift means for advertisers, publishers and rivals. It builds on our earlier look at Alphabet’s Q3 revenue and profit picture , and it separates hard numbers from speculation throughout. Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. The core statement is short. Schindler said on the call that “the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.” The line, captured by Search Engine Roundtable , is rare for an earnings call. Executives usually frame new products as pure upside. Here Google named a specific product and said it earns less than the one it partly replaces. Google tied the gap to two things. AI Mode shows fewer ads than a classic results page, and the advertising value per query is lower. Both points matter. Fewer ads means fewer paid slots per search, and a lower value per query means each slot is worth less to the advertiser. Together they explain why strong usage growth in AI Mode can coexist with slower revenue growth in Search. Google did not publish the size of the gap. Ars Technica, The Register and Search Engine Land all reported the admission, and none of the coverage pins down a per-query revenue difference. That number remains unconfirmed, and any article that cites a precise percentage for it is guessing. The headline figures show a business that is still growing fast overall. Alphabet reported $127.6 billion in total Q3 2026 revenue, a 25% jump from a year earlier. Within that, Google Search and other advertising brought in about $63.3 billion, up 12%. Search is growing at about half the pace of the company as a whole, which is the gap analysts focused on. Search Engine Journal reported that Search growth slowed from 14.5% in the comparable prior-year quarter to 12% this time. Search Engine Land, which covered the call in detail, headlined its report around AI Mode’s lower monetization slowing Search ad growth. The stock reaction followed. Our own coverage of the 9% slide after the EPS miss shows how quickly the market priced in the concern. The table shows the pattern. Everything with a dollar sign is confirmed. The one number people most want, the exact monetization gap, is the one Google withheld. Classic Google Search was built around a results page with several ad slots, each tied to a keyword auction. A shopper typing a product name saw a stack of sponsored listings, then organic links. AI Mode works differently. It answers in a conversational format, often in a single synthesized response, so the page has less room for ads and fewer natural spots for them. The query mix also differs. Schindler said many AI Mode searches are upper-funnel, meaning the user is researching rather than ready to buy. He put it this way: “On AI Mode, many of these queries are upper funnel queries, allowing us to capture new, high-value commercial intent.” The line comes from the earnings call transcript carried by Yahoo Finance. A person asking about insurance options or comparing product categories has commercial intent, but not the immediate purchase intent that commands the highest click prices. Google confirmed that AI Mode carries fewer ads than traditional Search. That alone cuts revenue per query even if every individual ad earned the same as before. The company’s fix targets this directly by scaling ad placements within the AI formats. Google also pointed to lower advertising value per query. Earlier-stage research queries attract lower bids than “buy now” queries. As AI Mode absorbs more of the research phase, the average value of a query slips unless Google finds ways to monetize the follow-up questions that come next. Google’s response is to expand AI Mode ads, not retreat. The company said it is scaling ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode to more users and more queries, including international markets. extraction.body: The numbers $127.6 billion: Alphabet’s Q3 revenue, up 25% from $102.3 billion during the same period last year. Under analyst projections of $127.93 billion. $96.3 billion: Revenues from Google Services, which includes advertising, subscriptions, digital content, and hardware. That’s up 11% year-over-year (YoY), attributed in large part to growth in the Google Search business. Ad revenues included $82 billion of the total, though that number was below analysts’ expectations of $83.5 billion. $30.7 billion: Google Cloud revenue, up 103% YoY as the company’s AI infrastructure business booms. $51.4 billion: Google’s capital expenditures for the quarter, spent primarily on AI infrastructure investments. The figure fell 26% due to an unrealized loss on Alphabet’s SpaceX stake, the company said. The watercooler talk Google’s parent company, Alphabet, reported third-quarter earnings Wednesday after the bell, a day after Google unveiled Genie 4, a realistic world model, and just hours after it debuted Gemini 4 Carbon, which the company bills as its “strongest model” yet. Google claims the AI system shows “significant gains” in agentic tasks and coding, as well as cybersecurity use cases including vulnerability detection. While Google barrels ahead with AI growth, growth in its core search business slowed, rising at 12%, compared with 17% in the second quarter. Google’s chief business officer, Philipp Schindler, attributed the slowing rate to foreign exchange rates and one-off ad spend dips in Asia-Pacific among advertisers impacted by the EU’s elimination of its de minimis exemption on low-cost imports. He also flagged that while users are increasingly using Google’s AI-powered search experience, AI Mode, that system has fewer ads baked in and therefore makes less money. “The strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact [on decelerating Google Search growth] because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI Mode,” Schindler said. Ad tests in AI Mode have returned “promising results,” Schindler said, and the company plans to scale ads in both AI Mode and AI Overviews to more users and across a wider range of queries. That includes expanding ads in AI Mode into international markets for the first time and launching multi-turn ads in AI Mode in the U.S. “To be clear, we feel very good about our trajectory here,” Schindler said, also noting that click-through rates for sponsored and organic product listings in AI Mode are “similar.” It was another attempt from the tech giant to assure Wall Street that its original search business is alive and well, even while the product morphs into dynamic, integrated, AI-powered experiences that increasingly chip away at web publishers’ traffic. (Today, some publishers are railing against Google’s practice of using the same web crawler for both search indexing and AI by opting out of Google Search altogether. Others are suing Google for allegedly suppressing their ad revenues.) On Google’s second-quarter earnings call in July, CEO Sundar Pichai claimed AI search was “sending billions of clicks to websites every week.” Today, there was no mention of publisher traffic. Search isn’t the only core area being overtaken by AI. Google leaders told investors that agentic commerce is an increasing focus for the business and noted that the open-source Universal Commerce Protocol already lets “hundreds of thousands of brands” like Nike, Chewy, and Tapestry switch on direct agent-led checkout. Advertisers already have access to a slew of AI-powered tools for campaign planning, creation, management, and optimization, which would appear to be performing well for Google. The company said that Gemini helped create 1.5 billion ad campaign assets during the quarter, up 7x YoY. Meanwhile, YouTube remains a major revenue machine at the heart of Google’s ad business. YouTube ads during Q3 grew 9% to $11.2 billion. Amazon is teaming up with YouTube Shopping and allowing creators in the U.S. market to tag Amazon products. The overarching story, however, remains Google’s staggering AI expenditures. As some analysts have pointed out, Alphabet has essentially transformed from a cash-printing ads business to a capital-intensive AI infrastructure company, taking on more debt to support some $1 trillion in contractual commitments that include both spending promises and backstops. The key question for Wall Street is whether Google will be able to justify these enormous investments. Google says it’s already secured $561 billion in future cloud revenue from customer contracts. But a major chunk is reportedly tied to a single customer: Anthropic committed to spend $200 billion with Google Cloud over five years, according to a May report from The Information. That setup could theoretically expose Google to greater risk; if Anthropic and other Google Cloud partners stumble financially, Google is likely to feel the pain.Also, Google recently started renting computing capacity from third-party providers to keep abreast of demand while it builds its own data centers. That expense will put pressure on margins in the short term, according to finance chief Anat Ashkenazi. Google did not adjust its full-year capex projections, and Ashkenazi said Google's capex is still expected to "increase significantly" in 2027. Google shares dropped roughly 11% in after-hours trading. The key quote Google is eager to explore advertising opportunities within agentic AI experiences. So we're really architecting these agentic workflows in a way that we can intentionally design the time and the space for users to explore those choices,” said Schindler. He added: “We’re actually confident that we can provide really interesting, compelling advertising models for agentic use cases.”

Most notably, Google is shifting to an AI search platform powered by Gemini models.
Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September.
But the company’s stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history.
In the last quarter, Google saw search grow by 12 percent versus last year.
Except that’s a much slower rate than previous quarters.
Growth in Q2 was 17 percent, and Q1 saw 19 percent growth over 2025.
So that’s the first problem, likely driven by more consumers using AI chatbots to find answers.
The other issue is that Google’s take on AI search isn’t pulling in revenue like standard web search yet.
According to Schindler, each AI Mode query earns less revenue compared to a similar web search—there are fewer ads, and they cost less to run.
Google is not slowing down—it’s only going to accelerate the shift toward more AI.
The loss actually increased from -$5.8 billion to -$9.06 billion, a situation that is directly attributable to Google’s runaway AI spending.
Google had capital expenditures of $51.4 billion in Q3 and says it still expects total 2026 spending to be between $195 billion and $205 billion.
In 2027, Google is targeting more than $300 billion of AI investment.
While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more.
Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02.
That’s about a billion more than analyst guesses.
As part of the financial disclosure, Google announced an expansion of ads in AI Mode.
If you do decide to dip into Google’s search chatbot, you’ll probably see more contextual advertising.
These ads will begin appearing in more international markets soon.
In the US, where AI Mode ads were already becoming commonplace, Google will implement multi-turn ads.
That means the sponsored links will change continuously as you engage in a back-and-forth with the robot.
CEO Sundar Pichai noted that these complex interactions are becoming more common as Google pushes more users toward AI Mode.
To support this continued spending, Google points to its cloud revenue more than doubling over the past year.
It’s easy to see why the company is so keen to keep expanding in AI based on that.
Countless AI startups pay to run models on Google’s infrastructure.
But even the larger AI firms are using venture cash to do it, and if that funding were to dry up, Google’s cloud revenues could go with it.
While Google’s investments ensure it still turns a profit, the trend of spending more than it earns on products and services (that negative cash flow) could come back to bite it.
Search growth is declining, and Google is placing all its eggs in the AI basket.
On the Q3 2026 earnings call on October 28, 2026, Philipp Schindler said the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of lower monetization.
It matters because Google Search remains the cash engine behind everything else the company builds, including the Gemini models that power its newest search products.
Here Google named a specific product and said it earns less than the one it partly replaces.
Google Search and other advertising revenue still hit roughly $63.3 billion, up 12% year over year, but the mix is shifting toward a format that pays less per question.
The headline figures show a business that is still growing fast overall.
Alphabet reported $127.6 billion in total Q3 2026 revenue, a 25% jump from a year earlier.
Search is growing at about half the pace of the company as a whole, which is the gap analysts focused on.
Google confirmed that AI Mode carries fewer ads than traditional Search.
The Register’s headline said Google is struggling to make AI Mode searches pay, a blunter read than the company’s own.
Adweek ran a similar angle, reporting that the stock sank as AI Mode pressured Search ad growth.
AdExchanger took a wider lens, asking whether Google is even an ad business anymore given the scale of its ad revenue.
Classic Google Search was built around a results page with several ad slots, each tied to a keyword auction.
His point is that Google is winning on engagement while paying a short-term price on revenue.
Ars Technica, The Register and Search Engine Land all reported the admission, and none of the coverage pins down a per-query revenue difference.
As of September 2026, ads in AI Overviews were eligible to appear above or below the feature in more than 200 markets.
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
“The strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact [on decelerating Google Search growth] because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI Mode,” Schindler said.
While Google barrels ahead with AI growth, growth in its core search business slowed, rising at 12%, compared with 17% in the second quarter.

Growth in Q2 was 17 percent, and Q1 saw 19 percent growth over 2025. Search revenue was also flat in Q3.

So that’s the first problem, likely driven by more consumers using AI chatbots to find answers. The other issue is that Google’s take on AI search isn’t pulling in revenue like standard web search yet. According to Schindler, each AI Mode query earns less revenue compared to a similar web search—there are fewer ads, and they cost less to run.

While Schindler suggested AI mode revenue was set to increase, he was also careful to control expectations. Advertisers may need time, he said, to understand the value in AI search ads. The company’s research reportedly shows that users find these ads more relevant and helpful than the ones they see in traditional search.

As part of the financial disclosure, Google announced an expansion of ads in AI Mode. If you do decide to dip into Google’s search chatbot, you’ll probably see more contextual advertising. These ads will begin appearing in more international markets soon. In the US, where AI Mode ads were already becoming commonplace, Google will implement multi-turn ads. That means the sponsored links will change continuously as you engage in a back-and-forth with the robot. CEO Sundar Pichai noted that these complex interactions are becoming more common as Google pushes more users toward AI Mode.

Google is not slowing down—it’s only going to accelerate the shift toward more AI. Like last quarter , Google reported negative cash flow in Q3. The loss actually increased from -$5.8 billion to -$9.06 billion, a situation that is directly attributable to Google’s runaway AI spending. Google had capital expenditures of $51.4 billion in Q3 and says it still expects total 2026 spending to be between $195 billion and $205 billion. In 2027, Google is targeting more than $300 billion of AI investment.

The company’s AI compute infrastructure doesn’t just power Gemini. Countless AI startups pay to run models on Google’s infrastructure. But even the larger AI firms are using venture cash to do it, and if that funding were to dry up, Google’s cloud revenues could go with it.

While Google’s investments ensure it still turns a profit, the trend of spending more than it earns on products and services (that negative cash flow) could come back to bite it. Search growth is declining, and Google is placing all its eggs in the AI basket. If spending on cloud services in the industry drops or search growth stalls, the company could be looking at a lot more red in its future.

extraction.body: Google told investors on October 28, 2026 that AI Mode queries earn less money than comparable traditional Search queries, and the company says more ads are the answer, Ars Technica reported . The admission came on Alphabet’s Q3 2026 earnings call. It matters because Google Search remains the cash engine behind everything else the company builds, including the Gemini models that power its newest search products. Philipp Schindler, Google’s chief business officer and a senior vice president, framed the issue in plain terms. Fast growth in AI Mode queries dragged on revenue growth because each of those queries monetizes at a lower rate today. Google Search and other advertising revenue still hit roughly $63.3 billion, up 12% year over year, but the mix is shifting toward a format that pays less per question. This article breaks down what Google actually confirmed, what it left vague, how the company plans to close the gap with more Google AI Mode ads, and what the shift means for advertisers, publishers and rivals. It builds on our earlier look at Alphabet’s Q3 revenue and profit picture , and it separates hard numbers from speculation throughout. Schindler said on the call that “the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.” The line, captured by Search Engine Roundtable , is rare for an earnings call. Executives usually frame new products as pure upside. Here Google named a specific product and said it earns less than the one it partly replaces. Google tied the gap to two things. AI Mode shows fewer ads than a classic results page, and the advertising value per query is lower. Both points matter. Fewer ads means fewer paid slots per search, and a lower value per query means each slot is worth less to the advertiser. Together they explain why strong usage growth in AI Mode can coexist with slower revenue growth in Search. Google did not publish the size of the gap. Ars Technica, The Register and Search Engine Land all reported the admission, and none of the coverage pins down a per-query revenue difference. That number remains unconfirmed, and any article that cites a precise percentage for it is guessing. The headline figures show a business that is still growing fast overall. Alphabet reported $127.6 billion in total Q3 2026 revenue, a 25% jump from a year earlier. Within that, Google Search and other advertising brought in about $63.3 billion, up 12%. Search is growing at about half the pace of the company as a whole, which is the gap analysts focused on. Search Engine Journal reported that Search growth slowed from 14.5% in the comparable prior-year quarter to 12% this time. Search Engine Land, which covered the call in detail, headlined its report around AI Mode’s lower monetization slowing Search ad growth. The stock reaction followed. Our own coverage of the 9% slide after the EPS miss shows how quickly the market priced in the concern. The table shows the pattern. Everything with a dollar sign is confirmed. The one number people most want, the exact monetization gap, is the one Google withheld. Classic Google Search was built around a results page with several ad slots, each tied to a keyword auction. A shopper typing a product name saw a stack of sponsored listings, then organic links. AI Mode works differently. It answers in a conversational format, often in a single synthesized response, so the page has less room for ads and fewer natural spots for them. The query mix also differs. Schindler said many AI Mode searches are upper-funnel, meaning the user is researching rather than ready to buy. He put it this way: “On AI Mode, many of these queries are upper funnel queries, allowing us to capture new, high-value commercial intent.” The line comes from the earnings call transcript carried by Yahoo Finance. A person asking about insurance options or comparing product categories has commercial intent, but not the immediate purchase intent that commands the highest click prices. Google confirmed that AI Mode carries fewer ads than traditional Search. That alone cuts revenue per query even if every individual ad earned the same as before. The company’s fix targets this directly by scaling ad placements within the AI formats. Google also pointed to lower advertising value per query. Earlier-stage research queries attract lower bids than “buy now” queries. As AI Mode absorbs more of the research phase, the average value of a query slips unless Google finds ways to monetize the follow-up questions that come next. Google’s response is to expand AI Mode ads, not retreat. The company said it is scaling ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode to more users and more queries, including international markets. In the words of the company: “We are now scaling high-quality ads within AI overviews in AI mode to more users and queries.” TechCrunch framed the move as a global expansion of AI search ads arriving just as core ad growth slows. Search Engine Journal reported that the expansion includes multi-turn ads in AI Mode for U.S. users. That format lets advertising opportunities continue through follow-up questions instead of ending after the first answer. It tackles the fewer-ads problem at its root, since AI Mode ads can now follow the conversation, because a conversation with five turns can now carry more than one commercial moment. Reporting also indicates that advertisers cannot target AI Overviews or AI Mode as separate placements. Existing negative keywords and brand exclusions still apply. That design choice keeps the buying workflow familiar and lets Google roll out inventory without forcing a new campaign structure on millions of accounts. Google also said early user research shows people find the ads in these AI-powered experiences relevant. Again, no numbers came with the statement. Treat it as a direction of travel, not an audited result. Wall Street read the call as a trade-off between usage and money. Andrew Boone, an analyst at Citigroup, said: “While query growth reached a five-year high, monetization appears to be challenged while search faces difficult comps.” CNBC carried the comment in its post-earnings analyst roundup. His point is that Google is winning on engagement while paying a short-term price on revenue. Schindler pushed the opposite framing. He said the majority of AI Mode queries are incremental, and in his words: “In addition, the majority of AI Mode queries are incremental, creating more monetization opportunities over time.” The claim is that AI Mode creates searches that would not have happened otherwise, so any revenue from them adds to the total instead of cannibalizing it. Google gave no incrementality data to test that assertion. The Register’s headline said Google is struggling to make AI Mode searches pay, a blunter read than the company’s own. Adweek ran a similar angle, reporting that the stock sank as AI Mode pressured Search ad growth. AdExchanger took a wider lens, asking whether Google is even an ad business anymore given the scale of its ad revenue. Adweek reported that Alphabet shares fell after the results. The drop connects two worries. Investors see Google spending heavily on AI infrastructure and want proof that AI products can pay it back. The AI Mode admission handed skeptics a concrete example of a new product earning less than the old one. Our breakdown of Big Tech’s AI spending and the Gartner risk estimate covers the wider capex debate. AI Mode follows the same arc with higher stakes. Instead of a smaller screen, the constraint is a single synthesized answer. The same playbook applies: build ad formats native to the new interface, prove they perform, then scale them. Multi-turn ads and sponsored product listings inside AI answers are that playbook in action. The difference this time is the cost side. Serving a generated answer generally takes more compute than serving a page of links. Google did not give a cost-per-query figure on the call, so the margin effect stays unknown. Lower revenue per query combined with higher serving cost is the scenario bears worry about, and the company has not yet shown data that rules it out. Google’s problem is unusual because it already owns a giant ad business. Standalone AI assistants face a different version of the same question. They lean on subscriptions and API fees, and ads remain a debate. Our guide to ChatGPT versus Claude pricing shows how far the subscription-first model has gone for those products. The contrast is useful. A subscription-led assistant collects money whether or not the user buys anything. Google collects only when someone clicks an ad, so it must find the commercial moment inside every conversation. That makes ad quality central to Google’s AI strategy in a way it is not for rivals. It also explains why Google stresses relevance and click-through rates, the metrics that govern how much advertisers will pay. Sundar Pichai, Alphabet and Google’s chief executive, said in his remarks on the quarter that Google is building a single experience across AI Overviews, AI Mode and traditional Search. If those three surfaces blend, the monetization gap between them should matter less over time, since ads can follow the user across all three. Advertisers cannot buy AI Mode as a separate placement, so the practical moves sit inside existing campaigns. Review shopping and product-feed quality first. Sponsored product listings are the format Google cited for strong early click-through, and clean feeds are the entry ticket. Check negative keywords and brand exclusions too, since they carry over into the AI surfaces. Finally, plan for more AI Mode ads volume, not less. Google said it is expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode to more users and queries. More inventory usually means more competition for placements and, over time, shifting prices. Marketers who test early collect data while rivals still guess. For AI builders, the lesson is that capability does not equal revenue. Google ships some of the most-used AI products in the world, and it still has to engineer a business model around them. Our report on Google Cloud’s 82% growth and Gemini’s 950 million users shows the usage side of that story. The Search admission shows the harder half, turning usage into margin. For publishers, the stakes rise with every point of AI Mode growth. If more queries end inside a synthesized answer, fewer users click through to source sites. Google did not discuss publisher traffic on the call, so this report cannot quantify the effect. The direction of travel, though, links ad scaling in AI answers to the open question of who gets paid when an answer replaces a click. extraction.body: The numbers $127.6 billion: Alphabet’s Q3 revenue, up 25% from $102.3 billion during the same period last year. Under analyst projections of $127.93 billion. $96.3 billion: Revenues from Google Services, which includes advertising, subscriptions, digital content, and hardware. That’s up 11% year-over-year (YoY), attributed in large part to growth in the Google Search business. Ad revenues included $82 billion of the total, though that number was below analysts’ expectations of $83.5 billion. $30.7 billion: Google Cloud revenue, up 103% YoY as the company’s AI infrastructure business booms. $51.4 billion: Google’s capital expenditures for the quarter, spent primarily on AI infrastructure investments. The figure fell 26% due to an unrealized loss on Alphabet’s SpaceX stake, the company said. The watercooler talk Google’s parent company, Alphabet, reported third-quarter earnings Wednesday after the bell, a day after Google unveiled Genie 4, a realistic world model, and just hours after it debuted Gemini 4 Carbon, which the company bills as its “strongest model” yet. Google claims the AI system shows “significant gains” in agentic tasks and coding, as well as cybersecurity use cases including vulnerability detection. While Google barrels ahead with AI growth, growth in its core search business slowed, rising at 12%, compared with 17% in the second quarter. Google’s chief business officer, Philipp Schindler, attributed the slowing rate to foreign exchange rates and one-off ad spend dips in Asia-Pacific among advertisers impacted by the EU’s elimination of its de minimis exemption on low-cost imports. He also flagged that while users are increasingly using Google’s AI-powered search experience, AI Mode, that system has fewer ads baked in and therefore makes less money. “The strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact [on decelerating Google Search growth] because of the lower monetization we are seeing in AI Mode,” Schindler said. Ad tests in AI Mode have returned “promising results,” Schindler said, and the company plans to scale ads in both AI Mode and AI Overviews to more users and across a wider range of queries. That includes expanding ads in AI Mode into international markets for the first time and launching multi-turn ads in AI Mode in the U.S. “To be clear, we feel very good about our trajectory here,” Schindler said, also noting that click-through rates for sponsored and organic product listings in AI Mode are “similar.” It was another attempt from the tech giant to assure Wall Street that its original search business is alive and well, even while the product morphs into dynamic, integrated, AI-powered experiences that increasingly chip away at web publishers’ traffic. (Today, some publishers are railing against Google’s practice of using the same web crawler for both search indexing and AI by opting out of Google Search altogether. Others are suing Google for allegedly suppressing their ad revenues.) On Google’s second-quarter earnings call in July, CEO Sundar Pichai claimed AI search was “sending billions of clicks to websites every week.” Today, there was no mention of publisher traffic. Search isn’t the only core area being overtaken by AI. Google leaders told investors that agentic commerce is an increasing focus for the business and noted that the open-source Universal Commerce Protocol already lets “hundreds of thousands of brands” like Nike, Chewy, and Tapestry switch on direct agent-led checkout. Advertisers already have access to a slew of AI-powered tools for campaign planning, creation, management, and optimization, which would appear to be performing well for Google. The company said that Gemini helped create 1.5 billion ad campaign assets during the quarter, up 7x YoY. Meanwhile, YouTube remains a major revenue machine at the heart of Google’s ad business. YouTube ads during Q3 grew 9% to $11.2 billion. Amazon is teaming up with YouTube Shopping and allowing creators in the U.S. market to tag Amazon products. The overarching story, however, remains Google’s staggering AI expenditures. As some analysts have pointed out, Alphabet has essentially transformed from a cash-printing ads business to a capital-intensive AI infrastructure company, taking on more debt to support some $1 trillion in contractual commitments that include both spending promises and backstops. The key question for Wall Street is whether Google will be able to justify these enormous investments. Google says it’s already secured $561 billion in future cloud revenue from customer contracts. But a major chunk is reportedly tied to a single customer: Anthropic committed to spend $200 billion with Google Cloud over five years, according to a May report from The Information. That setup could theoretically expose Google to greater risk; if Anthropic and other Google Cloud partners stumble financially, Google is likely to feel the pain.Also, Google recently started renting computing capacity from third-party providers to keep abreast of demand while it builds its own data centers. That expense will put pressure on margins in the short term, according to finance chief Anat Ashkenazi. Google did not adjust its full-year capex projections, and Ashkenazi said Google's capex is still expected to "increase significantly" in 2027. Google shares dropped roughly 11% in after-hours trading. The key quote Google is eager to explore advertising opportunities within agentic AI experiences. So we're really architecting these agentic workflows in a way that we can intentionally design the time and the space for users to explore those choices,” said Schindler. He added: “We’re actually confident that we can provide really interesting, compelling advertising models for agentic use cases.”

extraction.body: Information released by Distributed Denial of Secrets is the third such government data disclosure in the last month Information released by Distributed Denial of Secrets is the third such government data disclosure in the last month Data identifying more than 41,000 employees and contractors for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was released on Wednesday in an unprecedented leak that reveals how the agency is organized. The records, which were made public by the transparency non-profit Distributed Denial of Secrets, reference operation names, surveillance programs and information on undercover initiatives. The DHS did not immediately return a message seeking comment. The leaked data unveils the ​names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from various DHS agencies, including Immigration ‌and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border ‌Protection (CBP), Homeland Security Investigations and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Most of the agents in the leak – more than 21,000 – work for CBP, and about 6,600 work for ICE. The data also includes job titles, email groups and other details that show which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work. It was made public at a time when the DHS, in turn, has aggressively sought to unmask critics on social media, and obtain records on protestors and journalists – even as it moves to keep its own agents anonymous, defending their right to hide their identities and faces while conducting enforcement. In a statement, Emma Best, a Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder, said the hacktivist known as “maia arson crimew” developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would “replace anonymity with accountability” and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight. The disclosure – which the ⁠non-profit data transparency group says draws ⁠on information obtained ​by an entity calling itself “the Department of Peace” – is the third government data leak to have made headlines in the past month. The Department of Peace did not immediately respond ‌to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data, it said that DHS employees “have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped the data “can ​be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”. In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed ⁠the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the defense department was hit with ⁠a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel. The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking the DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors. Best’s statement said the Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by the DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: “Okta is ⁠secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised.” Reuters could not immediately ​verify the authenticity of the entire data ​trove but it was able to match ​personal information of about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data ​carried by the dark ‌web intelligence platform District 4 ​Labs. In other cases, ​Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach. In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees’ LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.

The database was briefly inaccessible on Thursday but was soon republished at a different domain.

A group calling itself "Department of Peace" claimed responsibility for obtaining the data, and said in a statement on Wednesday that DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs" and that it hoped the data "can be used to limit further harm ​by the DHS and supports all ​efforts in that direction."

Oct 29 (Reuters) - The US Department of Homeland Security asked an Icelandic hosting company on Thursday to take down or limit access to data related to thousands of agency personnel, saying the content put them at risk, according to the request posted online by hosting company FlokiNET.

FlokiNET CEO Kolja Weber told Reuters that his company would not remove the DHS data because it included government employee work addresses and work phone numbers, not personal phone numbers and addresses.
We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected.”
Privacy advocates have criticized DHS' use of personal data from other agencies, including Medicaid records and taxpayer data, for immigration enforcement.

extraction.body: Information released by Distributed Denial of Secrets is the third such government data disclosure in the last month Information released by Distributed Denial of Secrets is the third such government data disclosure in the last month Data identifying more than 41,000 employees and contractors for the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was released on Wednesday in an unprecedented leak that reveals how the agency is organized. The records, which were made public by the transparency non-profit Distributed Denial of Secrets, reference operation names, surveillance programs and information on undercover initiatives. The DHS did not immediately return a message seeking comment. The leaked data unveils the ​names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from various DHS agencies, including Immigration ‌and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border ‌Protection (CBP), Homeland Security Investigations and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Most of the agents in the leak – more than 21,000 – work for CBP, and about 6,600 work for ICE. The data also includes job titles, email groups and other details that show which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work. It was made public at a time when the DHS, in turn, has aggressively sought to unmask critics on social media, and obtain records on protestors and journalists – even as it moves to keep its own agents anonymous, defending their right to hide their identities and faces while conducting enforcement. In a statement, Emma Best, a Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder, said the hacktivist known as “maia arson crimew” developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would “replace anonymity with accountability” and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight. The disclosure – which the ⁠non-profit data transparency group says draws ⁠on information obtained ​by an entity calling itself “the Department of Peace” – is the third government data leak to have made headlines in the past month. The Department of Peace did not immediately respond ‌to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data, it said that DHS employees “have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped the data “can ​be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”. In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed ⁠the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the defense department was hit with ⁠a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel. The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking the DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors. Best’s statement said the Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by the DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: “Okta is ⁠secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised.” Reuters could not immediately ​verify the authenticity of the entire data ​trove but it was able to match ​personal information of about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data ​carried by the dark ‌web intelligence platform District 4 ​Labs. In other cases, ​Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach. In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees’ LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.

sources.title: Crypto worth billions frozen after suspected Binance hack - BBC
passages: Binance says crypto worth $6.3bn impacted in suspected hack
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have also frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."

Early checks show the suspected hack may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said in a series of online alerts.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of assets.
"It does look like a hack," Binance's former boss Changpeng Zhao said on X.
Binance said earlier that the amount of funds frozen may continue to increase while investigations are underway.
Binance, which was founded in China by Zhao in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The incident is potentially the biggest ever crypto heist, eclipsing a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, which was linked to North Korea.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses".

extraction.body: Binance is the world's biggest cryptocurrency trading platform Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of assets. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses". Early checks show the suspected hack may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said in a series of online alerts. The incident is potentially the biggest ever crypto heist, eclipsing a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, which was linked to North Korea. The security incident concerns Binance.com, while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US which provides trading services specifically for American residents, said its platform is not affected by the issue. "It does look like a hack," Binance's former boss Changpeng Zhao said on X. Zhao, who is also known as CZ, no longer manages the firm but remains a key shareholder. Binance said earlier that the amount of funds frozen may continue to increase while investigations are underway. "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice," Binance said, urging users to rely only on its official channels for updates. It added that it will release a full report once its investigation is complete. In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing their assets. Early checks show the suspected hack may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said in a series of online alerts. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that a "security incident" on its platform has impacted about $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of assets. "It does look like a hack," Binance's former boss Changpeng Zhao said on X. Binance said earlier that the amount of funds frozen may continue to increase while investigations are underway. Binance, which was founded in China by Zhao in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The incident is potentially the biggest ever crypto heist, eclipsing a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, which was linked to North Korea. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses". extraction.body: Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe. Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds. The company said it would publish a technical report, and an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation efforts. "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said. The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group , Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack. Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets. Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion." Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach. Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Later, Binance co-founder Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million of funds linked to the possible attack. But those frozen funds could represent only part of those impacted. Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin , ether , solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit. Arkham identifies, tracks and flags crypto wallets by analyzing publicly available blockchain data. It also solicits tips from its community members. Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. passages: Binance reported a potential security issue on October 30, 2026 and said it was investigating, while crypto firms froze more than $2.5 billion in related funds, according to the Associated Press .
The exchange has not explicitly confirmed that a hack took place.
Its founder, Changpeng Zhao, said publicly that the incident looks like one, and markets did not wait for a verdict.
The Binance security issue is still a developing story.
For the freeze breakdown by issuer, our earlier piece on who froze what, with Tether at $1.57 billion and Circle at more than $800 million , covers the ground.
A later report put the frozen total at $2.54 billion, and named Circle and Tether among the firms that froze related assets.
Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it ran security checks and worked with law enforcement.

O’Leary’s statement said Binance had “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.” The word temporarily helps, but it gives engineers no restart time.

A Binance spokesperson also leaned on reassurance: “Rest assured that user funds are completely safe.” The same statement added that “Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.” Engineers should note the promise to use official channels.
Frozen funds do not equal losses, and no verified source has stated an amount stolen or the method behind any unauthorized transfers.
Today that feed speaks of a potential issue and a precautionary pause, and neither maps cleanly to a boolean.

Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses.
Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident.
Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets.
Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday.

"We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak.

extraction.body: Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses. The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe. Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds. The company said it would publish a technical report, and an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation efforts. "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said. The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group , Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack. Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets. Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion." Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach. Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Later, Binance co-founder Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million of funds linked to the possible attack. extraction.body: Binance reported a potential security issue on October 30, 2026 and said it was investigating, while crypto firms froze more than $2.5 billion in related funds, according to the Associated Press . The exchange has not explicitly confirmed that a hack took place. Its founder, Changpeng Zhao, said publicly that the incident looks like one, and markets did not wait for a verdict. Bitcoin slid to a six-week low of $77,646, and Ether fell to a two-month low of $2,238.76. BNB, the exchange’s own token, dropped more than 8% over 24 hours to $694, CNBC’s market coverage showed . Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while it ran security checks and worked with law enforcement. Most coverage treats this as a trading story. This analysis takes the engineering angle instead: what a Binance security issue and a withdrawal pause do to bots, payout systems, treasury scripts and any code that treats one exchange as a dependency. For the freeze breakdown by issuer, our earlier piece on who froze what, with Tether at $1.57 billion and Circle at more than $800 million , covers the ground. Here the question is narrower and more practical: what should software teams change before the next incident? Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Start with the confirmed layer, because it is thinner than the headlines suggest. Binance said it had flagged a potential security issue and that its teams were investigating. It said cryptocurrency firms had frozen more than $2.5 billion in funds, a figure that the Atlanta Journal-Constitution carried from the AP report . A later report put the frozen total at $2.54 billion, and named Circle and Tether among the firms that froze related assets. Binance also said it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks. A spokesperson, Ross O’Leary, described the move as a precaution on multiple networks following a security incident. Beyond that, the company promised updates through its official channels once information is verified. Now the unconfirmed layer. Binance has not said that a hack occurred. No outlet in the verified set has a confirmed figure for any amount stolen. The method behind any unauthorized transfers remains unreported. A frozen balance is also not a loss figure, since freezing stops funds from moving and says nothing about how much already left. Readers who want the gap between early estimates and the frozen total can read our breakdown of the $5.7 billion estimate versus the $2.54 billion frozen . That distinction matters for engineers because incident language drives automated decisions. A bot that parses an exchange status feed can only act on what the feed says. Today that feed speaks of a potential issue and a precautionary pause, and neither maps cleanly to a boolean. The price moves were sharp but not catastrophic. Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 in Friday trading and touched a six-week low of $77,646 along the way. That low sits roughly $350 below the Friday print, so the two numbers describe the same slide at different moments rather than two different events. Ether and BNB took the heavier hits in percentage terms. Ether’s two-month low matters for developers who build on it. Lower prices shrink on-chain fee revenue in dollar terms and squeeze projects that hold treasuries in ETH. Bitcoin’s six-week low, by contrast, mostly rattles derivatives desks and anyone running leveraged strategies. Keep in mind that these are market prices on a volatile day. A decision to cut or add exposure on a six-hour chart is a trading call, not an engineering one. The freezes tell the clearest story about who holds power in a crisis. Tether froze about $1.57 billion in USDT. Circle froze more than $800 million in USDC. Those two actions show that stablecoin issuers can lock tokens at the contract level, fast, and without waiting for a court. The arithmetic raises a fair question. The two named issuers add up to roughly $2.37 billion, while the later report totals $2.54 billion. Binance’s statement spoke of cryptocurrency firms in the plural. We cannot say which firm froze the remainder, and no outlet in our verified set itemized it. Treat the difference as an open item rather than a finding. For developers, the lesson is structural. A stablecoin balance is a claim on an issuer that keeps a freeze switch. That switch protects users when thieves move funds and it also means your treasury’s liquidity depends on a third party’s judgment. If your app settles in USDT or USDC, your risk model should include tokens frozen at the issuer as a named failure mode, alongside smart contract bugs and depegs. A fair reader may ask why a story about a crypto exchange sits in the software section. The answer is dependency. Thousands of small teams run code that talks to exchanges: market-making bots, arbitrage scripts, payout services for gig platforms, tax tools that pull trade history, price feeds that feed other apps. When a major venue halts withdrawals, every one of those systems inherits the outage whether its authors planned for it or not. Our software coverage usually asks how a tool behaves under stress. This event fits that frame, because the stress test arrived unannounced. The earlier Binance explainer on custody lessons from the $2.5 billion freeze argued that users should separate what a platform says from what its systems prove. Engineers can apply the same discipline to integrations: trust a status page less than a health check you wrote yourself. There is also a sober business point. Teams that build on a single exchange concentrate counterparty risk in one API key. Today’s incident is a reminder that an exchange being down and an exchange being insolvent are different states, and your code usually cannot tell them apart in real time. Ledger jobs often assume that a withdrawal request becomes a confirmed transfer within a predictable window. A pause breaks that assumption and leaves pending states that never clear. Reconciliation code needs an explicit stuck status with an owner and a timeout, so finance teams can see which balances are exposed instead of finding out at month end. O’Leary’s statement said Binance had “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.” The word temporarily helps, but it gives engineers no restart time. Build for an open-ended pause and treat any resumption as a bonus. The list below reflects our editorial judgment, not a standard and not anything Binance has recommended. Each item targets a failure mode described above. Effort ratings are rough guesses for a small team with existing infrastructure. Pair the gate with a kill switch that an operator can flip from a phone. During a fast-moving event, the person on call needs one action that halts new orders across all strategies. Test that switch monthly, because untested kill switches tend to fail on the day they matter. Security scares attract opportunists. Fake support messages, cloned login pages and bogus compensation links tend to appear within hours of any large incident. Teams should assume that staff who hold exchange credentials will receive phishing attempts today and brief them accordingly. Use official channels only, and verify any update against the exchange’s own announcements rather than a forwarded screenshot. Rotate API keys on any account that touches the affected venue, even if you see no sign of misuse. Remove withdrawal permission from keys that only need to trade. Enforce IP allowlists where the platform supports them. These steps cost little and shrink the damage if a key leaked through a separate path. The self-custody layer. Nobody can pause your wallet, which is the whole point. Nobody can recover it either. Key loss, phishing and bad backups become your problem. For teams, a split approach usually works best: keep operating capital where speed matters, and keep reserves in controlled self-custody with documented recovery steps. Binance’s first public line was short. A spokesperson said, “Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.” CNBC carried that statement in its coverage of the market reaction. The wording avoids the word hack and avoids any amount. A Binance spokesperson also leaned on reassurance: “Rest assured that user funds are completely safe.” The same statement added that “Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.” Engineers should note the promise to use official channels. Subscribe to those channels and nothing else. Changpeng Zhao went further than the company did. In reporting by CoinDesk and Cryptowisser, Zhao said, “It does look like a hack on Binance.” He also said, “User funds are safe.” A third remark came with a caveat about his role: “I don’t manage Binance anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Read those lines carefully. Zhao is Binance’s founder and a former CEO who says he no longer manages the exchange, so his words carry weight in the market but do not amount to a company finding. The company itself has stayed with the word potential. That gap between founder and firm is the reason the unconfirmed list in the first section still applies. The immediate market impact came through sentiment, not through confirmed losses. Bitcoin’s six-week low and Ether’s two-month low show that investors treated a single-venue scare as a sector risk. That makes sense. Many traders and developers rely on Binance, so doubt about its custody practices can ripple through liquidity, spreads and funding rates. Second-order effects matter for builders. Lower prices cut the dollar value of on-chain activity, which can pressure revenue for projects that charge in percentage terms. Wider spreads raise the cost of automated trading. Exchanges competing with Binance may see inflows, though inflows also bring their own operational strain, and the outcome depends on how users judge each venue’s controls. A caution on timing: predictions about a live incident age fast. If Binance confirms a hack or rules one out, revisit the whole list. The Binance security issue is still a developing story. What is confirmed fits in a paragraph: a reported potential issue, an investigation, a temporary pause on deposits and withdrawals, more than $2.5 billion frozen (a later report says $2.54 billion), and sharp price drops across Bitcoin, Ether and BNB. What is not confirmed, including whether a hack occurred, the amount stolen and the method, will decide how this ends. Engineering teams cannot control that outcome. They can control how much a pause costs them. Cap balances, gate trading on venue health, scope and rotate keys, hold an off-venue float, and write the freeze runbook now. Do those five things and the next headline becomes an inconvenience instead of an outage. Did Binance confirm it was hacked? No. Binance reported a potential security issue and said it was investigating. Changpeng Zhao said the incident looks like a hack, but the company has not explicitly confirmed one. How much money was frozen? Binance said cryptocurrency firms had frozen more than $2.5 billion in funds. A later report specified $2.54 billion in frozen crypto assets, with Circle and Tether among the firms that froze related assets. How much was stolen? That is unconfirmed. Frozen funds do not equal losses, and no verified source has stated an amount stolen or the method behind any unauthorized transfers. How far did the Bitcoin price fall? Bitcoin dropped to a six-week low of $77,646 and traded down more than 4% at $77,994.96 in Friday trading. Ether hit a two-month low of $2,238.76, and BNB fell more than 8% over 24 hours to $694.
